summary: INT8 quality concerns for summarization workload (enterprise prospect) — guidance + eval sign-off
environment: prod (evaluation via Hosted API; customer workload representative set)
description:
Issue summary
NordicBank (enterprise prospect) is evaluating quantized inference for a summarization-heavy workload and raised concerns that INT8 may degrade output quality (faithfulness, omissions, formatting stability). They are requesting: (1) Redwood’s recommended INT8 eligibility criteria for summarization, (2) what evals Redwood requires before enabling INT8 by default, and (3) mitigation/fallback options if they want INT8 cost wins but cannot accept quality regressions.

Customer context
- Workload: document + meeting-note summarization with compliance requirements (high sensitivity to hallucinations / missing key facts).
- Prompt characteristics: long inputs (often multi-page), explicit formatting requirements (bullets + action items), occasional citations/quoting.
- Success criteria (as stated): match baseline quality closely; regressions that change meaning are unacceptable.

Observed symptoms (customer-reported)
- On a small internal sample set (n~50), INT8 outputs had:
  - slightly higher rate of missing named entities and numeric details
  - occasional deviation from requested structured format
  - a few examples of paraphrases that changed meaning
Customer is not sure if this is model variance, sampling, or quantization artifacts.

Impact
- Sales cycle risk: customer may rule out INT8 (and potentially Redwood) if we can’t provide a defensible evaluation approach + safe rollout guidance.
- No production incident; evaluation-stage only.

Requested from Redwood
- Provide recommended eval plan (what to measure, how to A/B, how many examples, what thresholds).
- Provide guidance on when INT8 is recommended vs FP8 vs baseline (BF16/FP16), and how to configure guardrails (fallback/rollout/canary).

Internal notes (do not forward verbatim)
- Summarization with long-context is one of the higher-risk classes for aggressive quantization. We should bias toward FP8 or baseline unless they can tolerate slight quality deltas.
- Align response to internal FP8/INT8 profile policy and avoid making external benchmark claims without the required footnotes.

Created from prospect thread routed via Solutions Eng: NordicBank asking whether INT8 is safe for summarization and what Redwood’s sign-off looks like. Assigning to Olivia (quality signals) and tagging Arjun (quant profiles) + Jonas (eval sign-off owner) for a crisp, consistent answer.

Customer quote excerpt (paraphrased): “We can trade a small amount of stylistic variation, but we cannot accept meaning changes or missing key items in summaries. Is INT8 recommended, and how do we validate?”

Questions for Arjun/Jonas:

2026-02-19 13:22Z — Arjun Desai
INT8 policy reminder: we treat summarization (esp. long-context, citation-like prompts) as “eval required” before enabling defaults. For hosted, INT8 is generally opt-in and guarded by shape/model constraints; FP8 is preferred when available on H100-class GPUs for better quality retention.

For customer guidance: recommend INT8 only with (a) calibration appropriate to model family, (b) prompt-set coverage of long docs, (c) explicit regression checks for numbers/entities, (d) fallback routing on quality/latency signals.

I’ll send Olivia the allowed external phrasing (high-level) and what we should not promise.

2026-02-19 14:10Z — Jonas Weber
Agree. For enterprise/prospect: require eval sign-off for enabling INT8 in any “default” configuration in their environment. Minimum eval set: their own golden set + Redwood sanity suite style checks.

Suggested rubric:
- Faithfulness / factual consistency (human or LLM-judge with strict guidelines)
- Entity + number preservation checks (heuristic + spot-check)
- Format adherence (JSON/schema or bullet structure)
- Long-context slice (p95 input length)

If deltas are localized, we can propose mitigations (prompt constraints, lower temperature, structured output, fallback).

2026-02-20 09:40Z — Olivia Grant
Sent customer-facing guidance (via Henry) — summary below for record:

1) Recommendation
- For high-stakes summarization, we recommend treating INT8 as “opt-in, eval-required.” Where available, FP8 is often a better first choice to capture most performance/cost wins with lower quality risk.

2) Suggested evaluation plan (A/B)
- Compare baseline (BF16/FP16) vs INT8 using the same prompts, same decoding params, and fixed seeds where possible.
- Use at least 200 examples; ensure coverage of:
  - long documents (top 20% input length)
  - numerically dense content
  - named-entity heavy content
  - strict formatting requirements
- Metrics / checks:
  - Faithfulness rubric (human spot-check of 30–50 samples; optional LLM-judge scoring for scale)
  - Entity/number preservation: track mismatches (simple extraction + diff)
  - Format adherence: schema validation / regex checks
  - Drift analysis: cluster failures by doc length and topic
- Acceptance guidance: no increase in “meaning-changing” errors; entity/number mismatch rate must not increase beyond a small agreed threshold on the golden set.

3) Mitigations if INT8 shows regressions
- Prefer FP8 for long-context summarization if supported on target SKU.
- Reduce decoding entropy (temperature/top_p) for summarization.
- Add explicit constraints: “do not infer, only summarize stated facts,” required sections, structured output.
- Use staged rollout with fallback: enable INT8 for a limited cohort; automatically fall back to baseline on detected regressions (error-rate/latency/quality signals if they have them).

4) Redwood support offer
- Under NDA, Redwood can help run a pilot evaluation with their prompt set and provide a short readout + configuration recommendation.

Also included note: we can share methodology and their own numbers, but we won’t provide blanket “INT8 is safe” claims without workload-specific evaluation.

2026-02-21 16:18Z — Henry Cho
Customer replied: they can provide ~500 anonymized documents + gold summaries for a pilot, but asked for a quick “go/no-go” on using INT8 for long-context (8k–16k tokens input). They also asked whether we have a fallback that can switch per-request.

Open questions to close:
- Confirm what per-request / per-route fallback options we can describe externally.
- Decide whether to recommend “FP8 only for long-context” as a simple policy, with INT8 limited to shorter inputs.

2026-02-23 11:03Z — Olivia Grant
Internal recommendation to Henry (for customer follow-up):
- For 8k–16k token input summarization, recommend FP8 (if on H100) or baseline, and treat INT8 as experimental until their pilot confirms no faithfulness regressions.
- Fallback: we can configure routing/flags at the deployment/route level (and in some setups, policy-based routing by request attributes). Externally: describe as “staged enablement with automated rollback based on SLOs,” and offer to scope a route split (INT8 for short docs, baseline/FP8 for long docs) as the first safe step.

Next action: waiting on customer to send anonymized dataset + decoding params they use in production (temperature/top_p/max_tokens) so we can align eval conditions.
resolution: Pending — waiting on customer to provide evaluation dataset and decoding parameters. Redwood provided an INT8 eval plan, mitigation guidance, and recommended FP8/baseline for long-context summarization unless workload-specific eval passes.
